correctness.rationale: Writing the probability in the first state as x converts any 2x2 row-stochastic letter matrix to f_a(x)=q_a+(p_a-q_a)x; nonnegative determinant makes the update monotone. For acceptance in the first/second state, upper/lower envelopes optimize at each step. Their iterates form a monotone orbit, and active distinct affine functions must have strictly ordered slopes along that orbit, forbidding any return to a letter after a different active letter. A unique word forces strict action at each prefix. Conversely the explicit rational f_(a_i)(x)=(r+(i-1)eps)x+c−eps*sum_{h<i}T_h have ordered crossing thresholds T_i between baseline orbit points. The orbit error is <=1/(5000 n^2), strictly below the half-spacing 3/(64n); all f maps send [0,1] strictly inside (0,1) with positive slopes. The prescribed runs are the only greedy itinerary. Counting ordered distinct run labels and compositions gives the formula. Independently enumerated all run-distinct words q=2,3,4 through length 6 and matched the expression; this is corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: Gill’s 2024 theorem classifies unrestricted *binary* two-state PFAs and includes alternating motifs requiring orientation-reversing letters; it does not determine the all-alphabet orientation-preserving model. Kjos-Hanssen’s 2026 three-state upper bound supplies existence for unrestricted words, not a minimal-two-state constrained if-and-only-if theorem. Resultary adjacent decreasing-two-state parity-run obstruction concerns the opposite sign of determinant. The monotone-affine envelope formulation was explicitly compared. Best-of-knowledge passes; an older affine control/greedy-envelope theorem could contain a close equivalent.

value.rationale: The order-preserving determinant restriction is an intrinsic stochastic dynamics condition, not a mere arbitrary word subset, and admits a complete finite-alphabet structural classification with rational positive witnesses. Exact enumeration separates polynomially growing accepted families for fixed q from all q^n words, and also explains the new role of orientation reversal in unrestricted binary witnesses.

final_claim: For q>=2 and n>=1, a length-n word is uniquely maximized by a two-state probabilistic automaton with nonnegative determinants for every letter iff its maximal constant runs have pairwise distinct labels. Every admitted word has a strictly positive rational transition witness; the exact count is sum_m (q!/(q-m)!) binom(n-1,m-1).
limitations: Only nonnegative-determinant two-state PFAs; unrestricted negative-determinant machines can isolate recurring-letter words.
Witness isolation gaps and bit complexity are not optimized.
